title: Adaptive toggle evolution & client migration kit for streaming/tool-call structured outputs
creator: Aisha Gopal
description:
Purpose: Provide a prescriptive migration kit and operational play for rolling behavioral changes that affect streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. The kit must minimize customer breakage, accelerate client SDK migrations, and provide reproducible backcompat tests that exercise streaming+toolcall edge-cases.

Context: We are introducing a set of behavior flag changes to standardize structured-output schema negotiation and to fix long-standing streaming termination edge cases that cause downstream tool-call parsers to mis-interpret partial chunks. These changes improve correctness and long-tail cost, but risk client regressions in older SDKs and bespoke tool integrations. This ticket is the PM-facing orchestration: docs, migration guide, staged deprecation timeline, success signals, and the required acceptance criteria for engineering to implement the hooks and tests.

Goals:
- Define naming and lifetime for the behavior flags and an opt-in/opt-out progression plan.
- Produce a client migration kit (checklist + SDK snippets + example server-side fallback policies).
- Specify a backcompat test matrix and telemetry signals for automated gating (canary -> gradual ramp -> retire).
- Draft runbook for incidents caused by flag toggles and automated rollback triggers.

Out of scope: Implementing the runtime kernel changes themselves (tracked in ENG tickets), low-level quantization recommendations, or non-API surface UX changes to Console dashboards (though telemetry hooks should be available).
acceptance_criteria: Behavior flag naming convention documented and approved by API council (e.g., runtime.behavior.stream_terminator_v2, runtime.behavior.toolcall_schema_strictness)
Migration guide published with step-by-step SDK code samples for Node/Python/Go and example server-side fallbacks

Backcompat test matrix defined and implemented in the regression harness with at least 1k synthetic queries covering: short/long sequences, mid-stream toolcall invocation, truncated chunks, multi-turn KV cache reuse
Telemetry signals and dashboards created: compat_probe_mismatch, streaming_chunk_incomplete_rate, toolcall_schema_error_rate, migration_canary_sla_violations
Canary gating criteria defined (error rate thresholds, latency regressions, token delta billing anomalies) and tied to automated rollback action
Customer communication plan (emails, changelog, release notes, migration webinar) scheduled prior to first canary
Rollback plan and postmortem template included in runbook

migration_checklist: Audit existing endpoints for reliance on partial-chunk parsing or implicit stream termination tokens
Integrate SDK snippet that gracefully accepts both legacy and new structured-output envelopes
Add feature-flag controlled rollout in client: start with opt-in, shadow-run, then opt-out deprecation wave
Run the regression harness locally against production snapshots and compare tokenization/parse deltas
Verify telemetry events are emitted and surfaced to support before enabling flag at scale
test_matrix_summary: Dimensions: client SDK version, model family, sequence length buckets (0-256, 257-1024, 1025+), tool-call bound vs non-toolcall flows
Key scenarios: mid-stream tool invocation, nested structured outputs, function call with chunked arguments, repeated KV-cache resume across sessions
Failure modes to evaluate: malformed JSON from chunk boundaries, duplicate tool invocations, truncated finalizer frames
Target coverage: 1k synthetic conversations with seeded edge cases + 100 customer-simulation traces
runbook_outline: Pre-canary: validate migration harness pass rate >= 99% on staging
Canary rollout (0.5% traffic): monitor streaming_chunk_incomplete_rate and toolcall_schema_error_rate for 24h
If error_rate > 0.5% or latency P95 regresses by >20%: automatic rollback to previous flag state
During ramp: run shadow consumer that replays new envelopes to legacy parser to detect silent mismatches
Post-incident: collect trace IDs, token deltas, and produce a postmortem within 72h
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: legacy clients break parsing mid-stream -> Mitigation: backward-compatible envelope and server-side fallback adapter
Risk: noisy false positives in telemetry -> Mitigation: calibration period and paired shadow-run validation
Risk: customers with air-gapped/private deployments miss notices -> Mitigation: targeted outreach via account teams and extended grace periods
notes: Prefer conservative default: opt-in for new strict schema during the first release window; provide server-side leniency for one major client version back
We should include a small sample dataset of failing traces in the regression repo to speed triage
Coordinate with growth for a migration webinar focused on platform partners who embed tool-call workflows
